title: October jobs report lands this morning
summary: The government releases its monthly jobs report at 8:30 a.m. New York time today. Economists surveyed by CNBC expected only about 59,000 new jobs, a small number. Traders are also watching to see how the numbers shape the Fed's next move.
why: The jobs report shows how many people got hired last month. The Fed uses it to decide whether to raise, hold or lower interest rates. Rates matter because they change how much big, fast growing companies are worth to investors, so a surprise in either direction can move the whole market.

title: Fed keeps rates steady, but two officials wanted a hike
summary: The Federal Reserve left its main interest rate at 3.75% to 4% on October 28. The vote was 10 to 2. Two members would have raised it by a quarter of a point, and the Fed said inflation is still elevated.
why: The Fed is the group that sets the cost of borrowing money in the US. When some members want higher rates, it hints that rates could go up instead of down. Higher rates make safe bonds more attractive and can make stocks, especially expensive tech stocks, look less appealing.

title: Nasdaq falls 5.5% as AI chip stocks lead the drop
summary: The Nasdaq, an index full of tech companies, dropped 5.5% on Thursday and moved into what traders call correction territory. Chip makers were hit hardest. Market writers linked the fall to worries about AI rules and spending after the midterm elections.
why: A correction means prices have fallen about 10% or more from a recent high. Chip companies sell the parts that power AI, so when investors worry about AI, these stocks often move more than the rest of the market. It is also why owning many different kinds of companies can soften the bumps.
